hero.h1: Taped axial parts, cut, U-formed and presented without a hand.
hero.lead: Resistors, diodes, inductors and jumper wires arrive on bandoleer tape. What slows the line is the bench where someone trims the leads, bends them and hands each part to the machine. The SAF1001 indexes the tape with a hardened ratchet, confirms each part by fibre, cuts and U-forms the leads in one cylinder stroke and presents the part to the head.

duel.lead: Left: a reel on the bench, side cutters, a forming jig and an operator who hands each part over. Right: the SAF1001 tape path, ratchet indexing, fibre check, cutter and forming die, and the waste tape dropping out of the front.
duel.note: Schematic animation from the SAF1001 teach document and 3D model. The SAF1001 side runs at its published 0.8 s per piece; manual timing and stops are illustrative.

chapters.text: Manual: cut a part from the tape, bend both leads by hand or in a jig, hand it to the machine. SAF1001: a pneumatic cylinder drives a hardened steel ratchet into the tape perforations, an anti-reversal pawl holds position, the fibre confirms the part, and one cylinder stroke cuts and U-forms the leads.
One part every 0.8 s at ±0.3 mm, with air-pressure speed regulation.
High-carbon steel blades shear the leads from the carrier tape; the male die bends them over the female die into a U. Pin spacing is set by moving the forming die blocks.
EIA-296 bandoleer tape, 26 or 52 mm standard, 35 / 64 / 92 mm custom; resistors, diodes, inductors, capacitors and jumper wires, body 3×3 to 6×20 mm, leads 0.4 – 1.0 mm.
730 × 95 × 212 mm, 8 kg, 24 V, 0.4 – 0.6 MPa air, 8-core Ø16 mm aviation plug with request, part-present, cut-complete and tape-empty signals, or standalone.
1,000 consecutive feeds with no misfeed and 48 hours of continuous ageing without failure.

why.title: The tape is orderly. The bench is not.
why.lead: Axial parts ship on paper tape that protects long leads, but a person still has to cut, bend and present them unless the feeder does it.

cards.h: Every part passes through a hand
cards.p: Cutting, bending and placing each resistor by hand costs seconds the insertion head could spend inserting.

cards.h: Lead length and pin spacing drift
cards.p: A hand-bent U varies from part to part. A forming die sets the same pin spacing every cycle and compensates for springback.
The SAF1001 fibre sensor raises a tape-empty signal to the host, so a reel change is planned instead of discovered.

blogs.title: Eight engineering reads before your axial feeding trial

items.title: Measure the bandoleer before choosing the feeder
items.summary: Tape width, pitch and paper thickness decide the tray.
body: The SAF1001 handles EIA-296 bandoleer tape: 26 or 52 mm wide as standard, 35, 64 or 92 mm on a custom configuration, with paper thicker than 0.2 mm.
Send a length of loaded tape with the inquiry so the tray and guide are set to your real material.

items.title: Check the body and the lead, not only the value
items.summary: Body 3×3 to 6×20 mm, leads 0.4 to 1.0 mm.
body: Most 1/4 W and 1/2 W resistors, diodes, small inductors and jumper wires fall inside the published body range.
Heavy-gauge leads up to 1.0 mm are cut by the same mechanism; confirm unusual parts with samples.

items.title: Why a ratchet beats friction for tape
items.summary: Positive engagement does not slip on dust or oil.
body: A hardened steel ratchet engages the tape perforations and a secondary pawl stops the tape moving back on the return stroke.
Friction or roller drives can slip as tape material varies; positive engagement makes every feed the same length.

items.title: Set pin spacing once, repeat it every cycle
items.summary: Four screws and two die blocks.
body: Loosen the M4 locking screws on the cutter assembly, move the left and right forming die blocks to the required spacing, and re-tighten.
Record the setting per part number so the next changeover starts from a known value.

items.title: Let the fibre decide when the tooling fires
body: The fibre sensor confirms a part is in the cutting station before the cylinder fires, preventing dry-firing.
When it no longer sees parts it raises a tape-empty signal, so the reel change is planned.

items.title: Agree the four signals before the bracket
items.summary: Request, part present, cut complete, tape empty.
body: The SAF1001 talks to the host PLC through an 8-core 16 mm aviation plug, or runs standalone.
It needs 24 V, 1 A average and 3 A peak, and 0.4 to 0.6 MPa factory air.

items.title: A maintenance plan that fits on one card
items.summary: Daily, monthly, quarterly, twice a year.
body: Clean the chassis and tape track daily, lubricate the cutter slides monthly, re-tighten bolts quarterly and inspect air tubes and wiring twice a year.
If leads start hanging, check air pressure, clean the cutter channel, then sharpen or replace the blades.

items.title: Ask for a run record, not only a clip
items.summary: 1,000 feeds and 48 hours are the published baseline.
body: The SAF1001 passed 1,000 consecutive feeds with no misfeed and 48 hours of continuous ageing without failure.
For your part, agree the acceptance criteria and keep the accepted formed sample with the production record.
